problem: LSP / contract violation: the recorded adapter declares `cancellation: false` (line 97) yet implements the optional `cancel` member as a method that always throws. In this interface an absent `cancel` is how an adapter says 'unsupported' (types.ts:156; adapter-shutdown.ts:50 and controller.ts:422 both test `cancel === undefined`), so this adapter advertises cancellation to every caller that checks the member and then fails. The declared capabilities also make the header's purpose unreachable: the controller refuses any adapter without `cancellation` (and without `hierarchy` for coordinators) at controller.ts:239, so every spawn with adapterId `recorded` returns `adapter_unsupported` and the adapter can never 're-drive a coordinator's plan'.
impact: Through the base type, cancelPendingDispatches (adapter-shutdown.ts:54) takes the 'supported' branch and rejects on the first recorded dispatch; through the controller the adapter is never admitted at all. Users of the replay feature get a refusal or a thrown shutdown instead of a replay. Fix: omit `cancel` (or implement a no-op that resolves, since there is no provider work to stop) and set capabilities to what the controller requires, or document why the adapter is meant to bypass the controller.

problem: No per-dispatch error handling or timeout in the shutdown loop. One rejecting `adapter.cancel` (the external adapter's cancel is tested to reject, external-adapter.test.ts:281; the recorded adapter's always throws) aborts the whole loop: every later pending dispatch is never asked to stop and the partially built report is discarded. A cancel that never settles hangs the shutdown. The controller already solved this for the same operation (controller.ts:418-429: Promise.race with cancelCleanupTimeoutMs, catch per dispatch, mark unresolved); this function re-implements it without either guard and has no field for 'cancel failed'.
impact: The module's stated purpose is that a host abandoning a run 'must not leave provider work running behind a closed controller' (lines 1-3). With one failing adapter early in the sorted list, the remaining provider work is left running and the caller gets an exception instead of a report saying which dispatches were stopped. Fix: catch per dispatch, record failures in a `failed` list, bound each cancel with a timeout, or reuse the controller's cancellation path.

problem: Swallowed exceptions: both empty `catch` blocks (lines 43 and 49) turn every read failure (ENOENT, EACCES, EISDIR) and every JSON syntax error into `null`, and the only caller turns `null` into an empty recording (`?? []`, line 83). execute then answers every dispatch with `{ findings: [] }, recorded: false` (line 109). The doc comment (line 38) also understates the behaviour: it says null means 'missing or not a JSON array', not 'unreadable or malformed'.
impact: A typo in recordingPath or a truncated recording file makes a replay run 'complete' with zero findings for every task and no error anywhere, which is exactly the wrong outcome for a dry run or plan-eval replay whose job is to reproduce a prior run's output. Fix: return null only for ENOENT if absence is a supported case, and throw with the path and cause for anything else.

problem: Hidden side effect in a predicate (output argument): `isReplayableResult`, named and documented as a pure check, sorts `entry.scopeIds` in place. `RecordedEntry.scopeIds` is the only non-readonly field (line 24), made mutable for this. `scopesMatch` (line 74) silently depends on that sort having happened inside an unrelated predicate during index construction.
impact: Anyone who calls scopesMatch on an entry that did not pass through isReplayableResult, reorders the filter, or makes the field readonly gets order-dependent false mismatches. Normalise scopeIds once in loadRecordedResults (sorted copy) and keep the predicate pure.

problem: Comment does not match the branch it sits above. It says the branch handles 'a task the recorded run never reached', but the condition also covers an entity mismatch, a scope mismatch, and entries dropped as stale by isReplayableResult. It also claims 'the summary counts it', but no code reads `recorded: false`: writeReplaySummary summarises the recording file, not replay outcomes.
impact: The next reader believes stale or mismatched recordings are distinguishable and counted somewhere; they are silently folded into the same empty reply. State the actual cases, or emit a reason in metadata.
quote:
// A task the recorded run never reached replays as an empty reply flagged
      // `recorded: false`, so the replayed plan still completes and the summary counts it.

problem: Two inconsistent parsers for one file format. loadRecordedResults casts the parsed array to ReviewAgentStoredResult[] with no validation (a missing `scopeIds` throws a TypeError from the spread on line 57, a missing `taskId` throws later at line 66), while writeReplaySummary (lines 130-143) validates taskId, attempt and createdAt and throws descriptive errors. Read, parse and validate of the recording are written twice with different failure policies (null vs throw vs TypeError).
impact: A recording the summary rejects with a clear message is half-accepted by the adapter, and the two will drift further as fields change. Extract one `parseRecording(path)` that validates and returns entries, used by both.

problem: Magic number duplicated: the 7-day replay window is written inline twice (line 69 and line 151) and the hour conversion as 3_600_000 (line 150), with no named constant tying the adapter's cutoff to the summary's `stale` flag.
impact: Changing the window in one place makes the summary report entries as fresh that the adapter silently drops (or vice versa). Introduce e.g. `REPLAY_MAX_AGE_MS` and `MS_PER_HOUR`.

problem: Single-letter accumulator with a comment that exists only to explain the name, and the name it maps to is inaccurate: the report field is `confirmed` but the value counts cancel calls that resolved, not confirmed stops (the controller distinguishes these via timeout). Similarly `unknownAdapter` (lines 15, 42) holds dispatch ids, not adapters.
impact: Readers of AdapterShutdownReport must open the implementation to learn what the numbers and lists contain. Rename to e.g. `cancelledCount` and `dispatchesWithUnknownAdapter`, and drop the comment.
quote: let n = 0; // n is the number of dispatches whose adapter accepted the cancel

problem: Non-terminal status set re-declared and misnamed. RUNNING_STATUSES is the complement of store.ts:24 `TERMINAL` and of the controller's `terminal()` check, written out a third time; it also includes `queued`, which is not running and has no adapter work, contradicting both the constant name and the doc 'an adapter may still be working on'.
impact: Adding a status to ReviewAgentAssignmentStatus requires remembering this list; a queued dispatch is sent to adapter.cancel for work that never started. Derive it from the shared terminal set and name it for what it is (e.g. NON_TERMINAL_STATUSES).

problem: SRP: writeReplaySummary reads the file, validates each entry, computes derived rows, sorts, and writes an output file in one ~30-line function; its doc comment lists the three responsibilities ('Validates..., summarises... and writes'). The output path and file name are also hard-coded next to the input.
impact: The summary computation cannot be tested or reused without filesystem I/O, and validation is not shareable with the loader (see G6). Split into parse/validate, a pure `summariseRecording(entries, nowMs)`, and a thin writer.
quote: /** Validates the recording, summarises each entry and writes `replay-summary.json` next to it. */

problem: Four positional parameters, the last two adjacent strings (`runId`, `reason`) of the same type, with no options object.
impact: Call sites can swap runId and reason without a type error, and the dispatched cancel then carries the wrong run id. Use a named options object `{ adapters, pending, runId, reason }`.
